newsitem.title: UK: Bond loves Moneypenny shock as OO7 exhibition opens.
newsitem.headline: Bond loves Moneypenny shock as OO7 exhibition opens.

text.p: Moneypenny really did have an affair with 007, "Q" hates gadgets in real life and some Bond girls could not speak English and had to be dubbed with voiceovers.
The largest exhibition ever dedicated to the Britain's most famous spy, opening on Friday, offers a wealth of detail to fans of Bond -- James Bond.
Everything from the sinister golden gun from Goldfinger to 007's stylish Aston Martin in Thunderball and hitman Jaws' monstrous silver teeth from The Spy Who Loved Me are on show.

For the diehard fan an official 007 martini shaker, no stirrer, with two glasses can be purchased for 34.99 pounds ($57.55) at the giftshop at the Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds, northern England. An estimated one in four people on earth have seen a Bond film.

Some of the actors synonymous with the suave spy were on hand to discuss a favourite topic among cinema-lovers -- who was the best Bond? Wearing his trademark tweed suit with trousers pulled a little too high and white hair slightly dishevelled, "Q" -- or actor Desmond Llewelyn -- said Pierce Brosnan was his favourite.
"I'm an old man and just can't seem to remember my lines. Pierce is so helpful and sincere, he makes it fun," said the 82-year-old Llewelyn who has starred in 15 Bond films stretching back to 1963.
"But I must admit I hate gadgets. I can't even get into my hotel room unless it has a proper key and not one of those card thingies."
Lois Maxwell, who competed for Bond's attentions as Miss Moneypenny in 14 films, gave the woman's vote to Sean Connery.
"I just love Roger (Moore), but Sean was the best Bond because he had a dark menace about him that the women really loved," she said.
Asked about the romantic tension between Bond and the secretary, Maxwell winked. "They had it off time and time again. He always came back when he got tired of all those girls."

Maxwell last played the part in View to a Kill in 1985 and has done little acting since. "I don't regret it for a minute, I just wish I got five pence for every time a Bond film showed around the world. I'd be floating in money."
Llewelyn appears in the upcoming Bond film, Tomorrow Never Dies. "I never grow tired of it. I'm bloody lucky to be working at my age you know."
Asked about the film, "Q" revealed he goes undercover as a rental car agent. "They'd probably kill me if I said too much. I have read the script but I didn't really understand it."
The first Bond film, based on the novels by writer Ian Fleming, was Dr No in 1962. Since then 16 official 007 films have been made, grossing over one billion dollars at the box office.
